=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

## Buyer advice — Project Kestrel

**The Seller’s update should not be treated as an agreed or balanced package merely because it says so.** On the material supplied, there is no independent evidence that both deal teams approved these positions, and the Seller’s market assertions do not resolve whether they are appropriate for this transaction. We should check the negotiating record, but mark up the draft to protect the agreed AUD 24 million, debt-free/cash-free acquisition.

The most immediate concerns are: **completion with Riverlark debt and security still outstanding; an ineffective Bluefen consent condition; unidentified responsibility for completion bonuses; and broad limitations and disclosure provisions that could defeat otherwise valid claims.**

This advice is based on the Seller’s summary and disclosure letter, not the full SPA or underlying DD documents. The proposed drafting must be checked against those documents and the complete due diligence record.

## 1. Transaction-specific issues

| Issue | Buyer concern and reasoning | Recommended position |
|---|---|---|
| **Riverlark facility — approximately AUD 3.2 million** | A release *after* Completion leaves the Buyer owning a company with debt and potentially continuing security, contrary to the debt-free/cash-free baseline. The debt has not been repaid and no final discharge is included. | Require repayment at or immediately before Completion from the Seller’s proceeds, supported by a lender payout letter, binding release and discharge arrangements, with evidence of authority and registration steps. Reflect the payment in an agreed funds flow and the debt/cash adjustment, without double counting. Do not complete relying solely on a later promise to release. |
| **Bluefen — approximately AUD 3.6 million FY26 revenue** | A written consent alone may not satisfy the conditions in clause 11.3. Given the reported revenue concentration, a defective or conditional consent could materially impair the asset being acquired. The disclosure letter confirms neither final consent nor satisfaction of associated conditions. | Make Completion conditional on a valid, effective written consent on terms acceptable to the Buyer, with all relevant conditions satisfied or validly waived, and no materially adverse variation. Obtain the full consent and evidence before Completion. Address the consequences if it is not obtained by the long-stop date. |
| **Completion bonuses — AUD 420,000 plus possible on-costs** | The bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment, but are absent from the funds flow. The Buyer could indirectly bear them through the Company. Payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are not established. | Determine which bonuses vest and who pays them. Require Seller funding or a clear price/debt-like adjustment for the bonuses and applicable on-costs, with an agreed calculation and payment mechanics. Avoid double recovery through completion accounts or another adjustment. |
| **Ironquay IP — AUD 180,000 recorded open** | The transfer of SOW3 Project Materials is conditional on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. DD-010 records an open amount, but is not independent proof that it remains unpaid. A payment-only indemnity may leave the Buyer with defective ownership or other resulting losses. | Obtain payment verification and a confirmatory assignment or other satisfactory evidence of title before Completion. Expand the specific indemnity to cover losses arising from non-payment and any failure or challenge to ownership or use of the relevant materials, including reasonable remediation costs. Ensure its cap, duration and interaction with other limitations are expressly addressed. |
| **Export/privacy incident** | The known fact is delivery of a download link to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification obligations remain unresolved. The issue is not yet a confirmed breach or quantified loss, but could generate investigation, notification, remediation or third-party costs. General disclosure and knowledge exclusions could shift that risk to the Buyer. | Require prompt investigation and preservation of evidence, access and cooperation, and an update before signing/Completion. Consider a specific indemnity for the identified incident, covering reasonable investigation, notification, remediation and third-party liabilities, with suitable limitations. Do not represent the incident as a confirmed breach without evidence. |
| **Sandbar renewals — AUD 330,000** | The Seller calls them ordinary-course costs, but the disclosure does not establish timing, accrual, terminability or whether they are unavoidable. Their treatment could affect the price mechanics and working-capital position. | Review DD-008 and DD-011 together and determine each renewal’s timing, commitment and accounting treatment. Allocate any pre-Completion or debt-like liability consistently in the adjustment mechanism; do not assume all AUD 330,000 is an immediate Seller liability. |
| **Share title** | DD-012 supports that Harbourglass is the registered holder of 100%, but the register alone is not complete independent verification of title, encumbrances or the full issued capital. | Verify the register, capital and encumbrances and obtain properly executed transfers, required corporate approvals and releases at Completion. Require robust title, capacity and authority warranties with enhanced remedies. |
| **Office lease and Mossvale** | On the disclosed wording, the lease requires notification, not necessarily consent; Mossvale restricts assignment, not necessarily a share sale. Treating either as an established consent condition would overstate the evidence. | Check the full documents and any indirect change-of-control provisions. Schedule the lease notice and confirm whether the transaction triggers any Mossvale restriction. Escalate only if the underlying terms support it. |

## 2. SPA risk allocation

### General warranty cap, thresholds and time limits

The Seller proposes a **20% cap (AUD 4.8 million)**, a **AUD 25,000 per-claim de minimis**, and a **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, with only the excess recoverable. The cap and thresholds could leave the Buyer absorbing substantial loss; the basket is particularly Seller-friendly because the first AUD 250,000 remains irrecoverable even after it is crossed.

The Buyer should seek:

- a higher general warranty cap, calibrated to the diligence and risk allocation;
- a lower de minimis and a **tipping basket**, so qualifying claims are recoverable from the first dollar once the threshold is reached;
- a longer general warranty notification period than 18 months, sufficient to identify issues through an appropriate post-Completion reporting cycle; and
- express rules for aggregation, calculation and interaction with other remedies.

These are negotiating objectives, not assertions that a particular alternative is universally market standard.

### Fundamental, tax and IP protections

Applying the general cap and 18-month period to **title and capacity** is not acceptable for a purchase of the entire share capital. Seek a cap of at least the purchase price and a substantially longer survival period for fundamental warranties, with no de minimis or basket. Confirm appropriate treatment for fraud and deliberate misconduct.

Tax risks can arise or be assessed after the general warranty period. Seek a separate tax covenant/indemnity for pre-Completion tax, with a limitation period linked to relevant assessment periods plus a notification buffer, and a separately negotiated cap and exclusions. Similarly, assess whether core IP ownership warranties need enhanced duration or protection; the Ironquay-specific indemnity must not silently fall within the general warranty regime.

### All-claims limitation, exclusive remedy and non-reliance

The proposed wording applies limitations and exclusive-remedy/non-reliance provisions to **claims of any nature**. That could undermine specific indemnities, completion adjustments, tax recovery, title remedies and claims based on pre-contractual statements—not merely general warranties.

Push back on the blanket formulation. Allocate limitations **claim by claim**, expressly preserving the intended operation of:

- completion price adjustments and debt/cash mechanics;
- specific indemnities and the tax covenant;
- fundamental warranty claims and enforcement of completion obligations; and
- fraud and other deliberate misconduct, to the extent permitted by applicable law.

Review the full clauses together: a carve-out in one clause is insufficient if another provision takes the remedy away.

### Disclosure and Buyer knowledge

The Seller seeks to disclose the entire data room, accounts, registers and public records, while also excluding claims for matters known or merely **discoverable** by the Buyer or its advisers. Together, these provisions could make diligence materials a broad liability shield, even where the issue and its consequences were not clear.

Require disclosure to be **fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter**, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its relevance to the relevant warranty. Reject deemed disclosure of the whole data room and public registers. Limit any Buyer-knowledge qualification to actual knowledge of specifically identified individuals, without imputed adviser knowledge or a discoverability test.

Specific disclosed matters still need commercial resolution. In particular, do not accept disclosure of Riverlark, Ironquay or the incident as a substitute for the agreed completion protections or specific indemnities. Check that disclosure and knowledge do not qualify those protections.

## Recommended priorities

1. **Before signing or as express Completion conditions:** secure effective Bluefen consent and Riverlark repayment and release; verify Ironquay payment and IP title.
2. **Fix the economics:** allocate the AUD 420,000 bonuses and on-costs, address Riverlark in the funds flow and debt/cash adjustment, and determine the Sandbar renewals’ proper treatment.
3. **Preserve recourse:** reject blanket all-claims limitations; negotiate enhanced fundamental and tax protection and an effective Ironquay indemnity, and consider an incident-specific indemnity.
4. **Narrow disclosure and knowledge:** remove general data-room/public-record disclosure and the discoverability exclusion; require fair, specific disclosure.
5. **Complete targeted diligence:** resolve the incident investigation and verify title, underlying consent terms and the lease/Mossvale obligations. Cross-check every proposed carve-out against the complete SPA before issuing the mark-up.
